unit.why: A short anecdote: the Besht sees someone desecrate the Sabbath, searches his own deeds and finds a corresponding fault, with a moralizing explanation.
unit.boundary_note: next division is a parallel version of the same tale from another book

stories.start_quote: ואמרו מגידי אמת שפ״א ראה הבעש״ט
stories.summary_en: The Besht once saw a man desecrate the Sabbath, examined himself and found he had served a Torah scholar before learning Torah from him, which counts as desecrating the Sabbath because a scholar is likened to the Sabbath.

tags.why: Sabbath desecration is the trigger of the tale

quotes: והיינו חילול שבת כי ת״ח דומה לשבת
tags.why: violation of a prohibition and its hidden counterpart

quotes: פשפש ומצא בעצמו ששימש עם צורבא מרבנן
tags.why: the sight is realized as a sign of his own fault
brief anecdote with a homiletic explanation, quoted in a teaching anthology
the order of serving a scholar and learning Torah is at issue

missing_concepts: self-examination: seeing another's sin as a mirror of one's own
